fields.title: Thyroid cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Thyroid cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Thyroid cancer is one of the most treatable cancers, provided it is diagnosed in good time and treated properly. Israeli clinics offer a wide range of innovative approaches to treating this disease, with high success rates.

Diagnosis of thyroid cancer

  1. Ultrasound scan
    The main diagnostic method, allowing the structure of the thyroid gland to be assessed and nodules or other abnormalities detected.
  2. Fine-needle aspiration biopsy
    A method in which material is taken from suspicious nodules under ultrasound guidance for cytological examination.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Laboratory tests
    These include tests for thyroid hormones and antibodies, and measurement of thyroglobulin levels after treatment.
  4. Radioisotope scan of the thyroid gland
    Allows the functional activity of nodules to be assessed.
  5. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    Used to assess the extent of the disease where metastases are suspected.

Treatment of thyroid cancer

  1. Surgery
    Includes thyroidectomy (complete or partial removal of the thyroid gland), which is the main treatment.
  2. Radioactive iodine therapy
    Given after surgery to destroy any remaining cancer cells and thyroid tissue, and also to treat metastases.
  3. Hormone therapy
    Prescribed to suppress the production of TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone), which prevents any remaining cancer cells from growing.
  4. Targeted therapy
    Used to treat metastatic thyroid cancer, particularly where certain molecular mutations are present.
  5. External beam radiotherapy
    Used rarely, mainly to control locally advanced disease or where there are metastases in the bones.

Why patients choose Israel

  • Experienced specialists
    Israel is home to leading experts in oncology and endocrinology with many years of experience in successfully treating thyroid cancer.
  • Advanced technology
    Israeli clinics are equipped with modern diagnostic and treatment devices, which allows accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach
    Every patient is given a personal treatment programme that takes account of every feature of their condition and illness.
  • Multidisciplinary teams
    Specialists of various kinds take part in treatment, which ensures a comprehensive approach and makes the treatment process as efficient as possible.

Innovative treatments, the high professionalism of medical specialists and an individual approach to every patient make Israel one of the leaders in the treatment of thyroid cancer at international level.

fields.title: Lacrimal gland cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Cancer of the lacrimal gland is a rare but aggressive malignant growth that develops in the tear gland. These tumours may be primary, arising directly in the lacrimal gland, or secondary, spreading from other parts of the body. Lacrimal gland cancer can lead to various complications, including loss of sight and the spread of the cancer.

Diagnosis of lacrimal gland cancer

  1. Detailed review of the medical history:
    • The doctor gathers information about symptoms such as swelling or pain in the area of the lacrimal gland, changes in tear production, visual disturbance, and past medical history.
  2. Visual examination and palpation:
    • The doctor examines and feels the area of the lacrimal gland to identify abnormalities and signs of a tumour.
  3. Ophthalmoscopy:
    • Examination of the fundus and the structures of the eye to identify changes and abnormalities.
  4. Ultrasound examination of the eye:
    • Used to obtain images of the structures of the eye and establish the size and position of the tumour.
  5. Computed tomography (CT):
    • Produces detailed images of the eye socket and reveals the spread of the tumour into neighbouring structures.
  6. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    • Used for a detailed study of the soft tissues and to identify metastases.
  7. Biopsy:
    • Taking a sample of tissue from the tumour for histological examination and confirmation of the diagnosis.
      (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  8. Doppler ultrasound:
    • Assessment of the blood supply to the lacrimal gland and identification of possible vascular abnormalities.

Treatment of lacrimal gland cancer

  1. Drug therapy:
    • Chemotherapy: The use of cytostatic medicines to destroy cancer cells and shrink the tumour.
    • Immunotherapy: The use of medicines that stimulate the immune system to fight the cancer cells.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • Brachytherapy: Placing radioactive seeds directly in the tumour for local treatment.
    • External beam radiotherapy: Radiation directed at the tumour to destroy the cancer cells.
  3. Surgery:
    • Local resection: Removal of the tumour and some of the surrounding tissue.
    • Orbital exenteration: Complete removal of the contents of the eye socket, including the lacrimal gland, in the case of large tumours or where there is a risk of spread.
  4. Laser therapy:
    • The use of a laser to destroy cancer cells in small, superficial tumours.
  5. Photodynamic therapy (PDT):
    • Administration of a light-sensitive agent that is activated by a laser and destroys the cancer cells.

Advantages of treating lacrimal gland cancer in Israel

  1. A high level of professionalism:
    • Israeli doctors have deep knowledge and many years of experience in treating lacrimal gland cancer and other cancers.
  2. Modern equipment:
    • Clinics are equipped with advanced diagnostic and treatment devices, which allows highly accurate investigation and effective treatment.
  3. An individual approach:
    • Every patient is given an individual treatment plan that takes account of the nature of the condition and their general health.
  4. Innovative treatments:
    • The use of the most modern methods and medicines, including immunotherapy and photodynamic therapy.
  5. Comprehensive support:
    • Covers not only treatment of the underlying condition but also support for the patient's mental and physical wellbeing during treatment and rehabilitation.

Treatment of lacrimal gland cancer in Israel gives patients access to high-quality medical care and considerably improves both the outlook and their quality of life.

fields.title: Salivary gland cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Salivary gland cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the salivary glands is a rare condition affecting one of the salivary glands. Israel treats it using innovative approaches that combine the latest advances in medical science with an individual approach to every patient.

Diagnosis of salivary gland cancer

  1. Examination and palpation
    The doctor examines and feels the area of the salivary glands for growths and hardening.
  2. Biopsy
    Taking a tissue sample to confirm the diagnosis by histological examination.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Blood tests and tumour markers
    Blood tests for tumour markers help assess general health and identify possible metastases.
  4. Ultrasound scan
    Used to assess the structure and size of the salivary glands.
  5. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI): These methods allow the extent of the tumour to be assessed.
  6. PET-CT
    An integrated investigation combining PET and CT for a detailed examination, including assessment of the activity of the tumour and the search for metastases.

Treatment of salivary gland cancer

  1. Surgery
    The main treatment, aimed at removing the tumour together with part or all of the salivary gland.
  2. Radiotherapy
    May be used as an additional treatment after surgery to destroy any remaining cancer cells, or to treat tumours that cannot be removed.
  3. Chemotherapy
    Used in advanced cancer or where there are metastases.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    The newest treatments, aimed at destroying cancer cells with the greatest precision and minimal effect on healthy tissue.

Why patients choose Israel

  • Multidisciplinary teams
    Leading specialists in oncology, surgery, radiology and other fields work together to develop the best treatment plan.
  • A personalised approach
    All treatments are chosen with the particular features of the illness and the patient's wellbeing in mind.
  • Innovative methods of diagnosis and treatment
    Patients have access to the most modern technology and treatment techniques, which considerably improves the chances of successful treatment.
  • A high standard of medical care
    Israeli clinics are known for the quality of their service, attention to detail and care for patients' comfort.

Treatment of salivary gland cancer in Israel gives patients access to advanced medical technology and highly qualified care, with an individualised and comprehensive approach to every case.

fields.title: Thymus cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Thymus cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the thymus, also known as thymoma, is a rare tumour arising from the epithelial cells of the thymus — an organ that plays an important part in the immune system. Israel treats this disease using the most modern medical technology and methods, which provide a comprehensive approach and highly effective therapy.

Diagnosis of thymus cancer:

  1. Computed tomography (CT) of the chest:
    The main method of imaging the thymus, allowing the size and structure of the tumour to be assessed along with any spread into the surrounding tissues.
  2. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    Used for more detailed imaging of the soft tissues and structures.
  3. PET-CT:
    Helps identify distant metastases.
  4. Biopsy:
    Carried out to obtain tumour tissue, which is necessary for accurate histological diagnosis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  5. Laboratory tests:
    These include blood tests that can reveal abnormalities relating to the functioning of the immune system.

Treatments for thymus cancer:

  1. Surgery:
    • Thymectomy: Removal of the thymus and surrounding tissue. It may be radical or partial, depending on the stage of the cancer.
    • Extended surgical resection: Removal of the tumour together with part of the surrounding affected tissues or structures.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • Given after surgery to destroy any remaining cancer cells, or as the primary treatment for inoperable thymomas.
  3. Chemotherapy:
    • Used in advanced cancer or where surgery is not possible. It is effective in shrinking tumours before an operation or radiotherapy.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy:
    • Targeted medicines: Directed at the molecular and genetic abnormalities of the tumour.
    • Immunotherapy: Medicines that stimulate the immune system to attack the cancer cells, particularly relevant where immunological syndromes are present.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Oncologists, thoracic surgeons, radiologists and immunologists combine their efforts to deliver the best result.
  • Advanced medical equipment and treatments: The newest developments are brought into clinical practice.
  • Individualised treatment plans: Approaches adapted as closely as possible to the features of the illness and the patient.

Treatment of thymus cancer in Israel aims to give patients the longest and best possible life, minimise side effects and provide comprehensive support at every stage of the fight against the disease.
